plain: List every file in this folder — including hidden dotfiles — with permissions, owner, size, and date.
when: You're in a folder and something seems missing. Plain ls hides dotfiles like .env and .git.

flags.meaning: long format: permissions, owner, size, date

plain: Jump back to your home directory from anywhere.
when: You're deep in a folder tree and want to get back to your starting point.

plain: Print the full path of the folder you're currently in.
when: You opened a terminal and aren't sure where you are, or a script needs an absolute path.

plain: Search every file under the current folder for the word error, ignoring case, and show line numbers.
when: A log or codebase is too big to read, and you need to find where something is mentioned.

plain: Find files by name under the current folder — here, every .log file.
when: You know part of a filename but not where it lives.

flags.meaning: match the filename against a pattern

plain: Make a script executable so you can run it with ./deploy.sh.
when: You get 'Permission denied' when trying to run a script you just wrote or downloaded.

plain: Make a private key readable and writable only by you.
when: SSH refuses your key because it's 'too open' — this locks it down.

flags.meaning: owner read+write; group and others get nothing

plain: Delete a folder and everything inside it, with no confirmation and no trash bin.
when: You want to wipe a generated folder (build/, dist/, node_modules/) and rebuild it.

plain: Create nested folders in one command, and don't complain if they already exist.
when: You're setting up a project structure and don't want to cd into each level.

flags.meaning: create parent folders and ignore existing ones

plain: List every running process on the machine with its user, CPU, memory, and command.
when: Something is eating CPU, or you need the PID of a process to kill it.

flags.meaning: user-oriented format with CPU and memory

plain: Force-stop a process by its PID. -9 means 'don't ask, just die.'
when: A process is frozen or ignoring a normal kill. Get the PID from ps aux first.

flags.meaning: send SIGKILL: stop immediately, no cleanup

plain: Extract a .tar.gz archive into the current folder, listing files as they come out.
when: You downloaded a .tar.gz and need the files inside.

flags.meaning: verbose: list files as they extract
use the archive file that follows

plain: Open an interactive shell on a remote machine over SSH.
when: You need to run commands on a server or a lab VM.

plain: Copy a file to a remote machine over SSH.
when: You need to move a file to or from a server without opening an interactive session.

flags.meaning: use a non-default SSH port (capital P)
